previous_catalog_record.summary: 0-bg grid (size varies). Several ISOLATED connected motifs (bbox >=2x2). 1..6 of them are color 4 (the TARGETS); 0..5 are DISTRACTORS in other colors from {2,3,5,6,7,8,9}. Motifs are separated by a 1-cell halo so each is its own 4-conn component. Rule: take every color-4 component and paint its FOUR bounding-box corners ((r1,c1),(r1,c2),(r2,c1),(r2,c2)) with color 1; leave the rest of each motif as-is. Objects of any other color are left COMPLETELY unchanged. Net: only color-4 motifs get their bbox corners flagged in blue. (Was a tiny 6-8x8-10 grid with 1-2 motifs, color 4 only, no distractors.)

scope: Accepted generator repair; finite reviewer evidence, no new maintainer execution

sequential_dependency.intermediate: The completed Stage-A grid containing all newly derived blue corner quartets; the red selector has not yet framed anything.
sequential_dependency.step_a: For every yellow connected component, mark the four corners of its input-derived bounding box blue.
sequential_dependency.step_b: Scan right from the red selector to the first derived blue corner, recover the matching right and lower blue corners, and paint that selected box perimeter green while preserving blue corners.
sequential_dependency.why_b_depends_on_a: The selected box address exists only as blue corners created by Stage A. On the raw input the selector ray encounters no blue corner, so Stage B cannot identify or frame the target box.
